entities.blurb: Cut copper is an oxidizing metal block crafted from blocks of copper. Like other copper blocks, cut copper can be waxed to prevent oxidation.
entities.name: Exposed Cut Copper

entities.blurb: A cut copper slab is a decorative slab variant of cut copper that generates in trial chambers and is used for building. Unlike other types of slabs, cut copper slabs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Exposed Cut Copper Slab

entities.blurb: Cut copper stairs are a decorative stairs variant of cut copper that generate in trial chambers and are used for building. Unlike other types of stairs, cut copper stairs can oxidize over time.
entities.name: Exposed Cut Copper Stairs

entities.blurb: A lightning rod is a block that, with sky access, causes natural lightning strikes in a large area to only target itself. Getting struck by lightning causes it to emit a redstone signal and, if it is not waxed, also reduces its level of oxidation.
entities.name: Exposed Lightning Rod

entities.blurb: Farmland is a block created by using a hoe on most types of dirt, and is required to grow seeds, carrots, and potatoes. Water and rain can hydrate farmland, improving crop growth. It reverts to dirt if broken, landed on repeatedly or left dehydrated and unplanted long enough.
entities.name: Farmland

entities.blurb: Ferns are non-solid plant blocks found only in certain biomes and have the same characteristics as grass.
entities.name: Fern

entities.blurb: Fire is a non-solid block that can spread to nearby flammable blocks and destroy them.
entities.name: Fire

entities.blurb: Coral is a type of non-solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn. Each of them are vibrant and colorful, but turn gray when they die.
entities.name: Fire Coral

entities.blurb: A coral block is a solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Fire Coral Block

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Fire Coral Fan

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Fire Coral Wall Fan

entities.blurb: A firefly bush is a decorative plant that produces firefly particles around it when exposed to darkness.
entities.name: Firefly Bush

entities.blurb: The fletching table is a fletcher's job site block that can generate naturally in villages. It is used to turn an unemployed villager into a fletcher.
entities.name: Fletching Table

entities.blurb: A flower pot is a decorative block that can contain flowers, bamboo, saplings, cacti, mushrooms, fungi, and other small plants.
entities.name: Flower Pot

entities.blurb: A flowering azalea is a variant of azalea that counts as a flower for all purposes, including pollination by bees, except for crafting dyes.
entities.name: Flowering Azalea

entities.blurb: Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling-leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
entities.name: Flowering Azalea Leaves

entities.blurb: Frogspawn is a non-solid block laid by frogs when they are bred, which hatches into tadpoles over time. It cannot be obtained as an item or moved by a piston.
entities.name: Frogspawn

entities.blurb: Frosted ice is a translucent block created when a mob or entity wearing Frost Walker-enchanted boots moves over water. It cannot be obtained as an item and will quickly crack and melt if exposed to light or sunlight.
entities.name: Frosted Ice

entities.blurb: A furnace is a block with two functions: it can be used for either smelting or cooking, by placing fuel and an appropriate item inside together.
entities.name: Furnace

entities.blurb: Gilded blackstone is a variant of blackstone found exclusively in bastion remnants, that can drop itself or gold nuggets when mined.
entities.name: Gilded Blackstone

entities.blurb: Glass is a transparent solid block that can be dyed into stained glass, or crafted into tinted glass. It is also a versatile crafting ingredient used to craft harnesses, glass panes, beacons, daylight detectors, and End crystals.
entities.name: Glass

entities.blurb: A glass pane is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to glass blocks. It can be dyed into stained glass panes.
entities.name: Glass Pane

entities.blurb: A glow lichen is a non-solid, light-emitting block. It can generate, or be placed, on any side of a solid block. It primarily generates on the side of blocks in caves.
entities.name: Glow Lichen

entities.blurb: Glowstone is a light-emitting block found hanging from ceilings and overhangs in the Nether. It can be used as a crafting material, broken into glowstone dust, and is required to fuel respawn anchors.
entities.name: Glowstone

entities.blurb: A block of gold, internally known as a gold block, is a precious metal block equivalent to nine gold ingots.
entities.name: Block of Gold

entities.blurb:
Gold ore is a rare mineral block found underground that drops raw gold when mined with an iron pickaxe or better.
Deepslate gold ore is a variant of gold ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff.
entities.name: Gold Ore

entities.blurb: A golden dandelion is a craftable flower that can be fed to baby mobs to pause their aging, or resume it by feeding another one to the same baby mob. It does not generate naturally and can only be obtained through crafting or the wandering trader.
entities.name: Golden Dandelion

entities.blurb: Granite is a block of igneous rock, found in large pockets underground or in sulfur springs.
entities.name: Granite

entities.blurb: A granite slab is a decorative slab variant of granite that does not generate naturally and is used for building.
entities.name: Granite Slab

entities.blurb: Granite stairs are a decorative stairs variant of granite that generate in desert villages and are used for building.
entities.name: Granite Stairs

entities.blurb: A granite wall is a decorative wall variant of granite that generates in desert villages and is used for building.
entities.name: Granite Wall

entities.blurb: A grass block is a natural block that generates abundantly across the surface of the Overworld.
entities.name: Grass Block

entities.blurb: Gravel is a gravity-affected block found in the Overworld and the Nether. It is a source of flint, which has a chance to drop when gravel is broken.
entities.name: Gravel

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Gray Banner

entities.blurb: A bed is a dyeable utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night and change their spawn point to within a few blocks of the bed, as long as it is not broken or obstructed. Villagers sleep in beds at night and require spare beds to produce offspring.
entities.name: Gray Bed

entities.blurb:
A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced.
Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
entities.name: Gray Candle

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with Gray Candle

entities.blurb: Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
entities.name: Gray Carpet

entities.blurb: Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Gray Concrete

entities.blurb: Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Gray Concrete Powder

entities.blurb: Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
entities.name: Gray Glazed Terracotta

entities.blurb: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
entities.name: Gray Shulker Box

entities.blurb: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
entities.name: Gray Stained Glass

entities.blurb: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
entities.name: Gray Stained Glass Pane

entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: Gray Terracotta

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Gray Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: Gray Wool

entities.blurb: A grindstone is a block used to remove all enchantments (except for curses) from items, refunding some experience orbs. Additionally, it can  repair tools, weapons, and armor. It also serves as a weaponsmith's job site block.
entities.name: Grindstone

entities.blurb: Hanging roots are a natural decorative block found underground in the lush caves biome.
entities.name: Hanging Roots

entities.blurb: Hay bales are storage blocks equivalent to nine pieces of wheat. They are used as a crafting ingredient, to feed llamas and all living horse variants, reduce fall damage, and extend campfire smoke.
entities.name: Hay Bale

entities.blurb: A heavy core is a rare block that can only be obtained from ominous vaults found in trial chambers. It can be combined with a breeze rod to craft a mace.
entities.name: Heavy Core

entities.blurb: A heavy weighted pressure plate is a type of pressure plate that produces a redstone signal while one or more entities stand on it. Depending on how many entities are detected, the outputted signal strength will range from 1 to 15.
entities.name: Heavy Weighted Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A honey block is a storage block equivalent to the contents of four honey bottles. It is sticky, can prevent jumping, and can be used in conjunction with pistons to move blocks and adhered entities.
entities.name: Honey Block

entities.blurb: Honeycomb blocks are decorative blocks crafted from honeycombs.
entities.name: Honeycomb Block

entities.blurb: A hopper is a low-capacity storage block that can be used to collect item entities directly above it, as well as to transfer items into and out of other containers. A hopper can be locked with redstone power to stop it from moving items into or out of itself.
entities.name: Hopper

entities.blurb: Coral is a type of non-solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn. Each of them are vibrant and colorful, but turn gray when they die.
entities.name: Horn Coral

entities.blurb: A coral block is a solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.

entities.name: Horn Coral Fan

entities.blurb: Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
entities.name: Horn Coral Wall Fan

entities.blurb: Ice is a transparent block formed from frozen water, which it can melt into if broken or exposed to bright light. Its top face is slippery for most entities and causes ridden boats to move at high speeds.
entities.name: Ice

entities.blurb: An infested block is a stone, stone variant or deepslate block inhabited by a silverfish, which can break out if it is mined or a nearby silverfish is attacked. Infested blocks break more quickly, do not drop as items and can be safely cleaned of infestation using Silk Touch.
entities.name: Infested Chiseled Stone Bricks

entities.blurb: Iron bars are the iron variant of bars.
entities.name: Iron Bars

entities.blurb: A block of iron, known internally as an iron block, is a metal block equivalent to nine iron ingots.
entities.name: Block of Iron

entities.blurb: Iron chains are metal decoration blocks and the iron variant of the chain.
entities.name: Iron Chain

entities.blurb: The iron door is a variant of the door made of iron that can only be opened using redstone. Iron doors are more secure than wooden and copper doors because they cannot be opened by hand and cannot be broken by zombies. They are also more resistant to explosions, and immune to fire and lava.
entities.name: Iron Door

entities.blurb:
Iron ore is a mineral block typically found underground. It is a source of raw iron, which can be smelted into iron ingots. 
Deepslate iron ore is the deepslate variant of iron ore. It is found in deepslate layers.
entities.name: Iron Ore

entities.blurb: An iron trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be only opened using redstone mechanisms.
entities.name: Iron Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A jack o'lantern is a variant of pumpkin that emits light, and can be used to build golems.
entities.name: Jack o'Lantern

entities.blurb: A jukebox is a block used to insert and play music discs. Playing a disc causes it to produce a redstone signal and allows nearby allays to duplicate when given amethyst shards.
entities.name: Jukebox

entities.blurb: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
entities.name: Jungle Button

entities.blurb: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Jungle Door

entities.blurb: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
entities.name: Jungle Fence

entities.blurb: A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.
entities.name: Jungle Fence Gate

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Jungle Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling-leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
entities.name: Jungle Leaves

entities.blurb: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently nine types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, and pale oak; and two types of stems: crimson and warped. The upcoming third drop of 2026 introduces poplar as the tenth log type.
entities.name: Jungle Log

entities.blurb: Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 12​[until: Third Drop 2026]/13​[upcoming: Third Drop 2026] variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
entities.name: Jungle Planks

entities.blurb: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
entities.name: Jungle Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A sapling is a non-solid block that can be grown into a tree.
entities.name: Jungle Sapling

entities.blurb:
A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once.
Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.
entities.name: Jungle Shelf

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Jungle Sign

entities.blurb: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
entities.name: Jungle Slab

entities.blurb: Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
entities.name: Jungle Stairs

entities.blurb: A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Jungle Trapdoor

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Jungle Wall Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Jungle Wall Sign

entities.blurb: Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 11 types (12 in Third Drop 2026​[upcoming]): oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar​[upcoming].
entities.name: Jungle Wood

entities.blurb: Kelp is aquatic algae found in all oceans except for warm oceans, frozen oceans, and deep frozen oceans. It can be planted underwater and grows over time (though not forever) or from bone meal usage. Smelting it results in dried kelp, which is edible and craftable into dried kelp blocks.
entities.name: Kelp

entities.name: Ladder

entities.blurb: A lantern is a block that emits light. It is brighter than a torch, and can be placed on top of or hang from the bottom of most blocks.
entities.name: Lantern

entities.blurb: A block of lapis lazuli, internally known as a lapis block, is a mineral block equivalent to nine pieces of lapis lazuli.
entities.name: Block of Lapis Lazuli

entities.blurb:
Lapis lazuli ore, internally known as lapis ore, is the ore block from which lapis lazuli is obtained.

entities.name: Lapis Lazuli Ore

entities.blurb: Lava is a light-emitting fluid that causes fire damage, mostly found in the lower reaches of the Overworld and the Nether.

entities.blurb: A bed is a dyeable utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night and change their spawn point to within a few blocks of the bed, as long as it is not broken or obstructed. Villagers sleep in beds at night and require spare beds to produce offspring.
entities.name: Light Gray Bed

entities.blurb:
A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced.
Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
entities.name: Light Gray Candle

entities.blurb:
A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation.
A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
entities.name: Cake with Light Gray Candle

entities.blurb: Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
entities.name: Light Gray Carpet

entities.blurb: Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Light Gray Concrete

entities.blurb: Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.
entities.name: Light Gray Concrete Powder

entities.blurb: Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
entities.name: Light Gray Glazed Terracotta

entities.blurb: A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.
entities.name: Light Gray Shulker Box

entities.blurb: Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
entities.name: Light Gray Stained Glass

entities.blurb: A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.
entities.name: Light Gray Stained Glass Pane

entities.blurb: Stained terracotta is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.
entities.name: Light Gray Terracotta

entities.blurb: A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
entities.name: Light Gray Wall Banner

entities.blurb: Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.
entities.name: Light Gray Wool

entities.blurb: A light weighted pressure plate is a type of pressure plate that produces a redstone signal while one or more entities stand on it. Depending on how many entities are detected, the outputted signal strength will range from 1 to 15.
entities.name: Light Weighted Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A lightning rod is a block that, with sky access, causes natural lightning strikes in a large area to only target itself. Getting struck by lightning causes it to emit a redstone signal and, if it is not waxed, also reduces its level of oxidation.
entities.name: Lightning Rod

entities.blurb: A lilac is a tall flower that can be crafted into magenta dye.
entities.name: Lilac

entities.blurb: A lily of the valley is a flower often found in forested biomes that can be crafted into white dye and suspicious stew.
entities.name: Lily of the Valley

entities.blurb: A lily pad is a plant block found in swamps, mangrove swamps, and as fishing loot. It can only be placed on water or waterlogged blocks and can be stood on as a platform.
entities.name: Lily Pad

entities.blurb: A magma block is a light-emitting block found underwater in the Overworld, and commonly in the Nether. It deals burning damage while stood on, which can be prevented by sneaking. Underwater magma blocks produce bubble columns that pull entities downward and provide air.
entities.name: Magma Block

entities.blurb: A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
entities.name: Mangrove Button

entities.blurb: The wooden door is a variant of the door made of wood that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
entities.name: Mangrove Door

entities.blurb: A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
entities.name: Mangrove Fence

entities.blurb: A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.
entities.name: Mangrove Fence Gate

entities.blurb: A hanging sign is a variant of a  sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
entities.name: Mangrove Hanging Sign

entities.blurb: Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling-leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
entities.name: Mangrove Leaves

entities.blurb: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently nine types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, and pale oak; and two types of stems: crimson and warped. The upcoming third drop of 2026 introduces poplar as the tenth log type.
entities.name: Mangrove Log

entities.blurb: Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 12​[until: Third Drop 2026]/13​[upcoming: Third Drop 2026] variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
entities.name: Mangrove Planks

entities.blurb: A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
entities.name: Mangrove Pressure Plate

entities.blurb: A mangrove propagule is an amphibious sapling that can grow into a mangrove tree. They grow hanging from mangrove leaves when the leaves are bone mealed or when a tree is first created, but can only be obtained as items if fully grown.
entities.name: Mangrove Propagule

entities.blurb: Mangrove roots are blocks that form as part of mangrove trees. Unlike other see-through blocks such as copper grates, mangrove roots are capable of conducting redstone power.
entities.name: Mangrove Roots

entities.blurb:
A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once.
Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.
entities.name: Mangrove Shelf

entities.blurb: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.
entities.name: Mangrove Sign

entities.blurb: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
entities.name: Mangrove Slab
